svg.title: Shortest-Path Algorithms Competition — task, data and scoring
svg.desc: Fork the provided Dijkstra into solver.cpp and make it faster with identical output. Six graph families in two tiers: a committed dev tier and a downloadable scored tier whose sizes are final. One program, grade.py, builds and times the foundation, runs your solver, checks the answers and computes the score.
svg.text: Make Dijkstra faster — the task, the data, and how you are scored
grade.py compiles it itself to measure T_base — editing
it means editing your own baseline.
Header V E FLAGS — bit0 coordinates, bit1 directed
when directed, u v w is the arc u → v only
Integer coordinates; weights fit in int32
Distances do not always fit in 32 bits
RULES — EVERY ONE OF THESE IS CHECKED
Derived from the foundation — submit the diff
3600 s per run — the foundation needs ≤ 26 min
First: make foundation && make check-data — both must pass.
foundation ≈ 1.65 h in total, ≤ 26 min each
THE SCORED TIER — SIZES ARE FINAL
Foundation time = unmodified dijkstra_foundation.cpp at -O2 on an Apple-silicon laptop,
≈ 1.65 h for the whole tier. Budget about 2× on an older machine.
A one-time setup cost has room to pay for itself.
Each instance ships a .meta.json with V, E, flags, weight range, query mix, unreachable count
and max distance — reason about the data instead of guessing.
ONE PROGRAM DOES ALL OF IT
You never time anything by hand and never run the
foundation yourself. Submit the result.json it writes.
builds the foundation at -O2, times it → T_base
extrapolated from two short query prefixes, not a full run
runs your solver three times → T_solver
checks your output against the shipped .answers
Score = geometric mean, on two tracks
Any failed instance scores 0.1 — and still counts.
It drags your geometric mean down; it is never quietly dropped.
Hidden test set — you get the full generator (tools/gen). Grading runs the same code with the same parameters and a seed you do not have: tune to the structure, not to the bytes.
Submit — solver.cpp and the result.json that grade.py writes. Nothing else.
